title: Define the session rules
prompt:
Marketing wants one row per visit: how long it lasted, what the visitor did, and whether they left after one page. The feeds deliver some events twice, and a few sessions lost their page views upstream.

Write `session_metrics(sessions, page_views, cart_events, checkout_events)`. Start from `parse_events(...)`, remove repeated deliveries, and return one row for every session in `sessions`.
rules: Two rows with the same `event_id` are one event. Count each event once.

Return `session_id`, `user_id`, `traffic_source`, `campaign_id`, `duration_s`, `page_views`, `cart_adds`, `orders`, `revenue` and `bounced`, one row per row of `sessions`. Events whose session isn't in `sessions` are left out.
`duration_s` is `ended_at` minus `started_at` in whole seconds. `page_views` counts page views, `cart_adds` cart events with action `add`, and `orders` checkout events with step `complete`.
`revenue` is the sum of those orders' `order_total`, each cast to DECIMAL(10,2), as DECIMAL(12,2): 0.00 when the session has no order. A session with no events has 0 in every count.
`bounced` is true when the session has exactly one page view. A session with no page views didn't bounce.
hints: `parse_events(...).dropDuplicates(["event_id"])` gives each event once. Group it by `session_id` and count with `F.count(F.when(condition, 1))`, which counts only the rows where the condition holds.
Join the per-session numbers to `sessions` with a left join, so sessions without events stay, then `F.coalesce(col, F.lit(0))` turns their missing numbers into 0.
`F.unix_timestamp("ended_at") - F.unix_timestamp("started_at")` is the length in seconds. Work out `bounced` from the page views after the coalesce, so a missing count isn't compared.
explanation: Removing repeats by `event_id` first means a page view delivered twice can't turn a bounce into a two-page visit, and an order delivered twice can't double the revenue. Conditional counts (`F.count(F.when(...))`) give every measure in one pass over the events. The left join from `sessions` keeps every visit, including those whose page views were lost and those with no events at all; `coalesce` gives them real zeros, so `bounced` is a clean true/false and revenue adds up as money. Casting each total to DECIMAL before summing keeps cents exact.
